bug_report_content:
id: 511
status: Fixed
summary: Last warning or error in output is truncated
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 11
Comment 0 (2011-07-12): The last error or warning statement written to the output appears to be getting truncated. It's causing a problem for my error / warning parser. To reproduce, create a file called test.js and add the following content to it: --------------- alert(foo); alert(bar); --------------- When compiled, the output looks like this: --------------- >java -jar compiler.jar --warning_level VERBOSE --js test.js test.js:1: ERROR - variable foo is undefined alert(foo); ^ test.js:2: ERROR - variable bar is undefined 2 error(s), 0 warning(s) --------------- If you look at the last error includes neither the line the error occurred on nor the column-indicating caret. This happens with warnings as well. Tested against r1257 committed 2011-07-11 11:11:32 -0700.
Comment 1 (2011-07-13): I tried and got the correct warning information: test.js:1: ERROR - variable foo is undefined alert(foo); ^ test.js:2: ERROR - variable bar is undefined alert(bar); ^ 2 error(s), 0 warning(s) Could you please try again and let me know if the error still occurs.
Comment 2 (2011-07-13): This is still happening for me as of r1261 with a stock build (no patches) on Windows 7 SP1. >svn up ... >ant clean ... >ant ... [created test.js file, as above] >java -jar compiler.jar --warning_level VERBOSE --js test.js test.js:1: ERROR - variable foo is undefined alert(foo); ^ test.js:2: ERROR - variable bar is undefined 2 error(s), 0 warning(s) >java -version java version "1.6.0_24" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.6.0_24-b07) Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 19.1-b02, mixed mode)
Comment 3 (2011-07-13): This doesn't appear to be a new issue at least. I can reproduce this in my environment going back to at least r500.
Comment 4 (2011-07-13): Another run against r1261, this time with two input files. It looks like it's cutting off the last error / warning for each input perhaps. >java -jar compiler.jar --warning_level VERBOSE --js test2.js --js test.js test.js:1: ERROR - variable foo is undefined alert(foo); ^ test.js:2: ERROR - variable bar is undefined test2.js:1: ERROR - variable foo2 is undefined alert(foo2); ^ test2.js:2: ERROR - variable bar2 is undefined 4 error(s), 0 warning(s)
Comment 5 (2011-07-14): I'm able to reproduce this on two other systems as well. Windows 7 SP1 >java -version java version "1.6.0_26" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.6.0_26-b03) Java HotSpot(TM) Client VM (build 20.1-b02, mixed mode, sharing) Windows Vista Business SP2 >java -version java version "1.6.0_22" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.6.0_22-b04) Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 17.1-b03, mixed mode) When building and running in Linux w/ Java 1.6.0_15 however, it seems to work. It may be strictly a Windows problem.
Comment 6 (2011-08-18): I can reproduce the problem in windows. I think the simplest workaround solution is to add a carriage return in the end of each input file.
Comment 7 (2011-08-18): maybe the output stream isn't being flushed properly?
Comment 8 (2011-08-22): It's fixed and will come with the next release.
Comment 9 (2011-08-23): This issue was closed by revision r1373.
Comment 10 (2011-09-07): Issue 414 has been merged into this issue.
